answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token before it may vote in a randomly sampled reputation committee. The protocol weights votes by locked stake and slashes that stake when an identity is caught endorsing the same fraudulent agent as its colluding peers. Creating a thousand aliases therefore requires a thousand funded bonds, while a coordinated fake identity risks losing them all; ember, fable, and yarrow can remain harmless labels rather than free influence.
